sections.skill: Explain how data quality and labels shape a model

questions.prompt: A model was trained on product prices from five years ago. Which data problem is this?

choices.text: Wrong labels
Outdated data
Missing data
Too many parameters

questions.correct_answer: Outdated data
questions.intro: A model can only learn what its data shows it, so DATA QUALITY matters as much as the model itself. Common problems: MISSING data (some cases never appear), WRONG LABELS (a cat photo labeled "dog"), OUTDATED data (prices from five years ago), and UNREPRESENTATIVE data (photos only from one country, voices only from adults). A LABEL is the correct answer attached to a training example, often added by people, and people make mistakes or disagree. Problems in the data become problems in the model, which is often summed up as "garbage in, garbage out."
questions.feedback: Old prices are outdated data.

questions.prompt: Many cat photos in a training set are labeled "dog." What will most likely happen?

sections.skill: Compare learning from a flawed map

questions.prompt: A map missing a neighborhood is like which data problem?

choices.text: Unrepresentative data
Wrong labels
Missing data
Outdated data

questions.correct_answer: Missing data
questions.intro: Imagine learning a city from a MAP. If the map is missing a neighborhood, you will never know it exists. If a street is labeled with the wrong name, you will confidently give wrong directions. If the map is twenty years old, you may send people to a store that closed long ago. If the map shows only the downtown, you will be lost in the suburbs. A model learns from its data the way you learn from the map: whatever is missing, wrong, old or one-sided in the data shows up in the model.
questions.feedback: Absent areas are missing data.

sections.title: Apply it

sections.skill: Handle hard data and labeling decisions

questions.prompt: Labelers disagree whether "not bad" is positive or neutral. What is the best step?

choices.text: Delete every review that is hard to label
Label every review "positive" to be safe
Let each labeler decide freely with no guidance
Write clear labeling instructions and check a sample

questions.correct_answer: Write clear labeling instructions and check a sample
questions.intro: Fixing data problems takes judgment. Some labels are hard because people genuinely disagree: is a review that says "not bad" positive or neutral? Writing clear labeling instructions and checking a sample of labels helps. Collecting more data does not help if the new data has the same gaps. And removing a column such as age does not always remove its influence, because other data can stand in for it. Good teams document where their data came from, what it leaves out and how labels were checked.
questions.feedback: Clear instructions and checks make labels consistent.
